title: Finite-stage etale Verdier biduality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites. Here $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ denotes the full subcategory of bounded constructible complexes having finite Tor amplitude: there are integers $u\leq v$ such that, for every sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules placed in degree zero, $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^LM)=0$ for $i\notin[u,v]$, using the ordinary etale Tor-amplitude definition [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

For every separated finite-type $X/k$, write $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for its structure morphism. The natural map

$$
\delta_K:K\longrightarrow D_XD_XK
\qquad(K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A))
$$

is an isomorphism. Here $D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$, $\omega_X=Ra_X^{\times}A$ is the ambient dualizing object, and $\delta_K$ is the transpose of evaluation, as specified in [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. Consequently $D_X$ is an exact contravariant anti-equivalence of $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$.

source.place: node thm-weil-etale-geometric-biduality, order 2128

proof.text: For the final specialization use the global finite-stage coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and the small etale categories, not the pro-etale or integral categories. The map is the transpose of evaluation from [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. Keep this coefficient ring fixed, but denote a variable algebraically closed geometric base field by $F$; it is not the global $k$ while the induction is running. Prove the assertion simultaneously over algebraically closed base fields of characteristic different from $\ell$, by strong induction on a dimension bound $d\geq0$: first prove it for proper schemes of dimension at most $d$, then for all separated finite-type schemes of that dimension. The empty scheme has only the zero sheaf and is immediate. Finite-type schemes over a field have finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] and are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. At $d=0$ every point is closed: a proper specialization would give a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length one. Thus the nonclosed-point part of the argument below is vacuous at the base of induction.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 1; supporting Stacks tags: 01T6

proof.text:
First establish preservation independently of biduality, for every algebraically closed field $F$ with $\operatorname{char}F\ne\ell$. Let $X/F$ be separated of finite type with $\dim X\leq d$ and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-sf-etale-smooth-stratified-ctf] to obtain the finite localization tower with pieces $Rs_!P$ on smooth strata $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ of pure dimensions $r\leq d$, where $P=s^{-1}K$ has local finite-projective models in $[a,b]$. Factor $s$ as $S\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{j}X$ with $i$ closed and $j$ open. The ordinary-etale clause of [lem-weil-delta-restriction] gives $j^*\omega_X\cong\omega_V$. The proper composition statement [lem-sf-unbounded-compact-support-proper-composition] applies to the closed (hence proper) immersion $i$ and the structure morphism $a_V$ over the actual field $F$. Together with the ambient adjoints [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, lem-exc-closed-ambient], it gives, for every ambient complex $C$ on $S$, the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C,Ri^!\omega_V)=\operatorname{Hom}(Ri_*C,\omega_V)=\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{V!}Ri_*C,A)=\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{S!}C,A)=\operatorname{Hom}(C,\omega_S).$$
Yoneda identifies $Ri^!\omega_V$ with $\omega_S$, including counits. Thus $Rs^!\omega_X=Ri^!j^*\omega_X\cong\omega_S$. Apply [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom], whose ordinary-etale clause is unbounded and assumes neither preservation nor biduality, to get
$$D_X(Rs_!P)\cong Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_A(P,Rs^!\omega_X)\cong Rs_*D_SP.$$
All schemes here are separated finite type over $F$, hence Noetherian; no step identifies $F$ with an algebraic closure of a finite field.

source.place: Agent expansion of imported Proof paragraph 3 and the predecessor preservation proof; ordinary-etale composition: Stacks 0F7J, 0F7B; smooth-stratum source: 09BI, 0B8X.

proof.text: For the smooth stratum $S/F$ of dimension $r$, [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] gives $\omega_S\cong L[2r]$, with $L$ etale locally free of rank one. Its Noetherian base is $\operatorname{Spec}F$, its structure map is smooth separated and compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification], and a power of $\ell$ annihilating $A$ is invertible in $F$. The local projective models of $P$ from step 2 have interval $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-sf-etale-local-dual-interval] with $m=2r$: $D_SP$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[-b-2r,-a-2r]$. This uses local coefficient dual models, with no biduality assumption.

source.place: Agent expansion of imported Proof paragraph 3 and lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata Proof; local finite-projective identity and localization; smooth ambient computation as thm-asd-smooth-tensor.

proof.text: For $s:S\to X$, [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] gives $R^qs_*M=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ and $q>2r$. Apply [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude] over this actual algebraically closed field $F$, with $N=2r$ and $G=D_SP$. The immersion is separated finite type, both schemes are finite type over $F$, and $A=A_{E,n}$ with $\ell$ invertible. The theorem's displayed all-sheaf vanishing predicate is precisely the bound just obtained, and does not restrict $F$ to the global finite-field closure. Thus $Rs_*D_SP$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[-b-2r,-a]$, contained in $[-b-2d,-a]$. This is the direct-image bound also used at stage 14--15.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-hom-triangulated] to each triangle of the finite localization tower of step 2. Starting from its zero end, the long cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] and Serre closure [thm-constructible-serre] give bounded constructible cohomology of $D_XK$. For every degree-zero module sheaf $M$, [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated] carries these same triangles to distinguished triangles after tensoring with $M$. Both end objects have cohomology zero outside $[-b-2d,-a]$, so their middle object does too by the long exact sequence. Induction along the finite tower gives this common Tor interval for $D_XK$. Taking $K=A_X$, which is locally free of rank one in degree zero, also proves $\omega_X=D_XA_X$ bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude. Preservation was obtained over every algebraically closed $F$ independently of double-dual isomorphisms.

source.place: Agent expansion of imported Proof paragraph 3 and lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata Proof; local finite-projective identity and localization; smooth ambient computation as thm-asd-smooth-tensor.

proof.text:
Fix a proper $X/F$ with $\dim X\leq d$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$. Set $\Delta=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta_K)$. By the arbitrary-base preservation proved in steps 2--5, both $D_XK$ and $D_XD_XK$ are bounded constructible. The long cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives, for each $q$, an exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal H^q\delta_K)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^q\Delta\longrightarrow\ker(\mathcal H^{q+1}\delta_K)\longrightarrow0.$$
By [thm-constructible-serre] its two end terms and hence its middle term are constructible. Outside a finite interval both end terms vanish. Thus $\Delta$ is bounded constructible; no finite-Tor assertion about the cone is needed.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 3; supporting Stacks tags: 05RS, 03RZ

proof.text: Suppose $d>0$ and $x\in X$ is nonclosed. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $x$, with finitely many $F$-algebra generators $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ of $B$. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field], $\operatorname{trdeg}_F\kappa(x)>0$. If every generator had algebraic image in $\kappa(x)$, the fraction field of their image algebra $B/\mathfrak p_x$ would be algebraic over $F$, a contradiction. Choose a generator $t=t_r$ with transcendental image. The coordinate morphism $p:V\to\mathbf A^1_F$ sends $x$ to its generic point, since $F[t]\to\kappa(x)$ is injective. The surjection $F[T_1,\ldots,T_m]\twoheadrightarrow B$ given by the generators gives a closed immersion $V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^m_F$. Apply [lem-fin-coordinate-generic-dimension] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$, $Y=V$ and its open subscheme $V$ itself; $\dim V\leq\dim X\leq d$ follows by viewing chains in an open subspace. Hence $\dim V_\eta\leq d-1$. By [lem-kun-dimension-extension] the same holds for $V_{\bar\eta}$ over $L=\overline{F(t)}$. This fibre is separated and finite type over $L$: on affine charts its rings are obtained from finitely generated $F[t]$-algebras by scalar extension, and its diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal of $V$; closedness survives scalar extension since $(R/I)\otimes_R R\prime=R\prime/IR\prime$ on affine charts.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 3

proof.text: Write $u:V\hookrightarrow X$ and $g:V_{\bar\eta}\to V$. Verify successively that $u^*K$ and $g^*u^*K$ meet the induction hypothesis's constructibility and Tor conditions. For each of the two pairs $(h,Q)=(u,K)$ and $(g,u^*K)$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies constant-$A$ module pullback $h^*$ with an exact inverse-image functor, so $\mathcal H^q(h^*Q)=h^{-1}\mathcal H^q(Q)$ and the finite cohomological range is preserved. By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-set-pullback] the pulled-back cohomology sheaves are constructible. On a stratum where a cohomology sheaf is a finite constant $A$-module, pull back its trivializing etale cover and its addition and scalar maps; the result is the same finite constant $A$-module on the pulled-back cover. Thus this is module constructibility, not only constructibility of sets. For a Tor interval $[a,b]$ of $Q$, [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] gives a flat complex $P$ supported in $[a,b]$, representing $Q$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], $h^*P$ has flat terms and is K-flat; it is still supported in $[a,b]$. Exactness of $h^*$ identifies its derived object with $h^*Q$, and the converse implication of [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] gives the same Tor interval. Applying these checks first to $(u,K)$ supplies the hypotheses for $(g,u^*K)$. Write $K_V=u^*K$. In particular $g^*K_V\in D^b_{ctf}(V_{\bar\eta,\Et},A)$. All cited pullback statements apply to arbitrary scheme morphisms; the geometric-generic morphism need not be finite type over the original $F$.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 4; supporting Stacks tags: 04JC, 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), 0G7E

proof.text:
Over the variable algebraically closed field $F$, put $L=\overline{F(t)}$ and $T=V_{\bar\eta}$. Choose finite generators of the affine $F[t]$-algebra of $V$ to obtain a closed embedding $i:V\hookrightarrow W=\mathbf A^r_{\mathbf A^1_F}$. After base change it is $i_L:T\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_L$. By [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], proper compact-support composition [lem-sf-unbounded-compact-support-proper-composition], and the ambient adjoints [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, lem-exc-closed-ambient], the same adjunction-and-Yoneda calculation as step 2 gives
$$\omega_V\cong Ri^!A_W(r+1)[2r+2],\qquad\omega_T\cong Ri_L^!A_{\mathbf A^r_L}(r)[2r].$$
The closed-support comparison [lem-sf-etale-generic-exchange-algclosed] applies with smooth integral curve $B=\mathbf A^1_F$ and bounded constructible input $A_W(r+1)[2r+2]$. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], its generic pullback is $A_{\mathbf A^r_L}(r+1)[2r+2]$. Apply [sk-lem-coprojection] with $K=A_{\mathbf A^r_L}(r)[2r]$ and invertible $L_0=A_{\mathbf A^r_L}(1)[2]$; these are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude since their sheaves are locally free of rank one. It gives an isomorphism
$$\theta:g^*\omega_V\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_T\otimes J,\qquad J=A_T(1)[2].$$
We only choose this isomorphism; evaluation compatibility below holds for any such choice.

source.place: Agent expansion of imported Proof paragraph 4: generic comparison computed from closed affine embedding, 0F09/0GIT/0A45 exchange, ambient affine adjunction and evaluation; no restricted generic-duality node is applied.

proof.text: The preservation argument above makes $\omega_V,K_V,D_VK_V$ bounded constructible over the actual $F$, the last two of finite Tor amplitude. Apply the internal-Hom clause of [lem-sf-etale-generic-exchange-algclosed] to $(K_V,\omega_V)$ and $(D_VK_V,\omega_V)$. It supplies isomorphisms $\beta$ satisfying its explicit evaluation equation. The inverse image $g^*=g^{-1}$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so it is its own derived functor, and it is strong monoidal by the canonical derived-tensor pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; this is the inverse-image tensor identification used in the evaluation equation of the generic exchange, and it is compatible with the symmetry because both sides are induced by the termwise sheaf tensor identity $g^{-1}(F\otimes G)\cong g^{-1}F\otimes g^{-1}G$ on K-flat representatives. Apply [lem-sf-etale-twisted-bidual-transport] with these comparisons and the preceding $\theta$, $Q=A_T(1)$ and $m=2$. Its invertible-factor cancellation identifies $g^*D_VD_VK_V$ with $D_TD_Tg^*K_V$ and carries the actual arrow $g^*\delta_{K_V}$ to $\delta_{g^*K_V}$. The latter is an isomorphism by the induction hypothesis over $L$, because $\dim T\leq d-1$ and stage 8 verified its constructible and Tor hypotheses. The ordinary-etale identity in [lem-weil-delta-restriction] likewise carries $u^*\delta_K$ to $\delta_{K_V}$ for $u:V\hookrightarrow X$. Thus the pullback of $\delta_K$ to $T$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Given a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ over $x$, the injection $F(t)\to\kappa(x)\to\Omega$ lets us choose $L$ inside $\Omega$ as the subfield algebraic over $F(t)$. This subfield is algebraically closed: a polynomial over it has coefficients in a finite algebraic extension of $F(t)$, so any root in $\Omega$ is again algebraic over $F(t)$. Hence $\bar x$ lifts to $T$ for this allowed choice of algebraic closure. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identify the cohomology stalks of the pulled-back cone with those of $\Delta$ at $\bar x$. They vanish because the pulled-back arrow is an isomorphism. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] then proves zero cohomology stalks at every nonclosed point.

source.place: Agent expansion of imported Proof paragraph 4: generic comparison computed from closed affine embedding, 0F09/0GIT/0A45 exchange, ambient affine adjunction and evaluation; no restricted generic-duality node is applied.

proof.text: For each of the finitely many nonzero $\mathcal H^q\Delta$, its support is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-support-constructible]; the preceding step shows it consists only of closed points (also at $d=0$). By [def-weil-constructible-subset] it is a finite union of locally closed subsets. Give each such subset its reduced locally closed subscheme structure. It is Noetherian, being a locally closed subspace of the Noetherian $X$, and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Each component has a generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. That point is closed already in $X$, so its closure in the locally closed subscheme is its singleton; hence each component is a singleton. Each support, and then their finite union $Z_0$, is therefore a finite set of closed points. This is the explicit finite-support argument, rather than an assumption that a constructible support is closed.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 4; supporting Stacks tags: 09YS, 005L, 0BA8

proof.text: Record the coefficient identification at $s=\operatorname{Spec}F$. In [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] take $F^{\rm sep}=F$ and the identity geometric point; the Galois group is trivial, so the equivalence is with abelian groups. Transporting the scalar endomorphisms $a\cdot(-)$ for $a\in A$, and their ring identities, gives an equivalence between small-etale constant-$A$ module sheaves on $s$ and $A$-modules. It is exact, since an equivalence of abelian categories preserves kernels and cokernels, and monoidal by [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar]. Apply the exact equivalence and its exact quasi-inverse termwise to complexes: they preserve acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms, hence induce inverse derived equivalences. The monoidal equivalence preserves flat objects and K-flat complexes because tensoring with an acyclic complex can be tested through either exact quasi-inverse. Thus the derived equivalence is monoidal; its tensor adjunction identifies derived internal Hom and its evaluation. For the structure map $\operatorname{id}_s$, use the compactification with both maps the identity in [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Extension by zero for the whole open is the identity by its presheaf formula [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]; direct image along the identity is the identity since $W\times_s s=W$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Therefore $R(\operatorname{id}_s)_!$ is the identity. Its right adjoint is the identity as well: the adjunction represents $\operatorname{Hom}(C,-)$ itself, and Yoneda gives the identification with the identity functor. Hence $\omega_s=A_s$. Consequently $D_s$ and its evaluation transpose [lem-weil-duality-pairing] are exactly derived coefficient duality and canonical coefficient evaluation under this equivalence.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 1; supporting Stacks tags: 04JQ, 03QT

proof.text: Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}F$ be proper. By [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], $R^ra_*M=0$ for all module sheaves and $r>2d$. Apply [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude] over $F$ with $N=2d$ and any Tor interval $[a_0,b_0]$ of $K$. Its hypotheses hold as in stage 3--5: $a$ is separated finite type, $A=A_{E,n}$ and $\ell$ is invertible in $F$. Thus $Ra_*K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude $[a_0,b_0+2d]$. Under the point equivalence of stage 13 its cohomology modules are finite: each finite stalk set is itself a finite generating list. The flat-model equivalence [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] gives a bounded flat sheaf representative on $s$; the exact monoidal point equivalence carries it to a bounded flat module representative. The finite ring $A$ is Noetherian (its ideals form a finite set), so [lem-pc-noetherian-flat-complex-perfect] makes this coefficient complex perfect. The canonical derived evaluation is therefore an isomorphism by the perfect-complex clause of [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius]. The point equivalence identifies this map with $\delta_{Ra_*K}$, including evaluation, as verified in stage 13. This replaces the inline signed double-complex calculation by existing coefficient lemmas.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5; supporting Stacks tags: 05SE, 05SU

proof.text: For the proper morphism $a$, [lem-weil-delta-proper-pushforward] identifies $Ra_*\delta_K$ with the isomorphism $\delta_{Ra_*K}$ just obtained. The additive left exact module direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] has a triangulated derived functor by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. It sends the cone triangle of $\delta_K$ to a triangle whose first arrow is an isomorphism. Its third object is therefore zero: $Ra_*\Delta=0$. This uses coefficient biduality at a point, without assuming geometric biduality on $X$.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5; supporting Stacks tags: 05SE, 05SU

proof.text: Put the reduced closed subscheme structure on $Z_0$ and write $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:X\setminus Z_0\hookrightarrow X$. For $M=\mathcal H^q\Delta$, its restriction $j^{-1}M$ has zero geometric stalks by construction of $Z_0$ and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. It is the zero sheaf by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Apply the recollement triangle of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] to $M[0]$. Its first term is zero and $i_*$ is exact, so the unit gives $M\cong i_*G$ for the degree-zero sheaf $G=i^{-1}M$. This derives the finite-support representation; the definition of support alone would not give this isomorphism.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5; supporting Stacks tags: 03Q1

proof.text: The reduced finite closed subscheme $Z$ is separated finite type over $F$ with dimension at most zero. The canonical degree-zero formula of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology] says $\Gamma(Z,G)=\prod_{z\in Z_0}G_{\bar z}$. It is $A$-linear because the canonical maps commute with the scalar endomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], these stalks identify with $M_{\bar z}$. The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], evaluated at the terminal object, gives $\Gamma(X,M)=\Gamma(Z,G)$. Moreover $\Gamma(Z,-)$ is exact on $A$-module sheaves: its formula is a finite product of exact geometric stalk functors [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and exactness of module sheaves is tested on underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $b=a i:Z\to s$, the point equivalence of step 13 identifies $b_*$ with this exact sections functor, so $Rb_*=b_*$. Since $i_*$ is exact, the ordinary-etale clause of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] gives $Ra_*M=Ra_*i_*G\cong Rb_*G=b_*G$. Thus $R^pa_*M=0$ for $p>0$ and, under the point equivalence, $a_*M=\prod_{z\in Z_0}M_{\bar z}$. This argument works in module sheaves directly and does not silently identify module-derived and abelian-derived cohomology.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5; supporting Stacks tags: 03Q1

proof.text:
Choose $a_0$ below the nonzero cohomology of $\Delta$. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], $\Delta$ has a cochain representative zero below $a_0$; concretely the good truncation has $\operatorname{coker}(d^{a_0-1})$ in degree $a_0$, the original terms above, and zero terms below, and the natural quotient map is a quasi-isomorphism because the discarded cohomology vanishes. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to that bounded-below representative and the left exact additive functor $v=a_*$ on $A$-module sheaves. Both categories of module sheaves are Grothendieck: use [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck] with the terminal index category and a universe in which each small etale site is small. The spectral sequence is therefore
$$E_2^{p,q}=R^pa_*(\mathcal H^q\Delta)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Ra_*\Delta).$$
By step 17 all columns with $p>0$ vanish. The bounded-below hypothesis supplies the theorem's finite, exhaustive, separated filtration in each total degree, so there are no convergence or extension ambiguities: $\mathcal H^q(Ra_*\Delta)\cong a_*\mathcal H^q\Delta$. Step 15 makes the left side zero. The point equivalence and step 17 then give $0=\prod_{z\in Z_0}(\mathcal H^q\Delta)_{\bar z}$. Each factor is zero, by its inclusion and projection in a finite product. Outside $Z_0$ the stalks were already zero. Stalk conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] gives $\mathcal H^q\Delta=0$ for every $q$, whence $\Delta=0$ by the definition of the derived category. Thus $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism for every proper $X$ of dimension at most $d$.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5

proof.text: Now let $X/F$ be any separated finite-type scheme with $\dim X\leq d$. Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to its structure morphism (the base $s$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated), obtaining a quasi-compact open immersion $j_0:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ with $\bar X$ proper over $F$, as in [def-nagata-compactification]. Replace $\bar X$ by the closed scheme-theoretic closure $C$ of $X$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], the resulting $j:X\hookrightarrow C$ is a quasi-compact dense open immersion. The closed subscheme $C$ remains proper: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $\bar X$, its coordinate rings are quotients of finite-type $F$-algebras, and after every base change the closed immersion remains closed: on affine charts a quotient $R/I$ pulls back to $R\prime/IR\prime$, whose image is the closed subset $V(IR\prime)$. Composing this closed map with the closed map supplied by properness of $\bar X$ proves universal closedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. These verify separatedness, finite type and universal closedness directly. By the dense-open clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension], $\dim C=\dim X\leq d$.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 2; supporting Stacks tags: 01W1

proof.text:
For $j:X\hookrightarrow C$, ordinary etale extension by zero is exact [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], so it preserves the cohomological range and $\mathcal H^q(j_!K)=j_!\mathcal H^qK$. On the finitely many constructibility strata of $\mathcal H^qK$, the extension restricts to the original finite locally constant sheaf; on the complementary closed subscheme it is zero, by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Those strata are locally closed also in $C$, since $X$ is open. Adding the complement gives constructibility in the ordinary-etale sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For any degree-zero module sheaf $M$ on $C$, exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] keeps $j^*M$ in degree zero, and the canonical ordinary-etale projection isomorphism [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] gives
$$(j_!K)\otimes_A^L M\cong j_!(K\otimes_A^L j^*M).$$
If $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, exactness of $j_!$ shows the right side has zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$. Hence $j_!K$ is bounded constructible of the same Tor amplitude. The existing open tensor lemma supplies the hidden flat-extension argument without introducing a pro-etale comparison.

source.place: Agent expansion of imported Proof paragraph 2: ordinary etale exact extension and stalk formulas, Stacks 03S5, 03DJ and 03TT; same Tor interval through the ordinary-etale open projection isomorphism. No pro-etale comparison is invoked.

proof.text: The proper case at bound $d$, proved in stage 18, gives an isomorphism $\delta_{j_!K}$. Restrict along $j$ and use the ordinary-etale clause of [lem-weil-delta-restriction]: its canonical comparison $(D_X\alpha_{j_!K})^{-1}\circ\alpha_{D_Cj_!K}$ carries $j^*\delta_{j_!K}$ to $\delta_{j^*j_!K}$. Here $j$ is an etale $F$-morphism of separated finite-type schemes and the finite coefficient exponent is invertible in $F$. For an etale $W\to X$ viewed over $C$, the formula [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] has exactly one summand, namely $K(W)$, since the factorization through the open is unique. At $d=0$ steps 7--11 were vacuous and steps 12--21 prove the base; for $d>0$ the only smaller-dimension use was stage 9--11 over $\overline{F(t)}$.
